discovery.title: Astronomers trace a record-distant radio burst
discovery.summary: A team reported tracing a fast radio burst that traveled for more than 10 billion years before reaching Earth, offering a rare probe of the early universe.
discovery.why_it_matters: Such signals can help researchers study distant galaxies and the material spread between them, turning brief cosmic flashes into tools for mapping the universe.

discovery.title: A temporary liquid may help make better solar cells
discovery.summary: Researchers reported a crystallization technique for perovskite materials that uses a temporary melting liquid and produced more uniform, less-defective materials in lab-made solar cells and LEDs.
discovery.why_it_matters: More durable, efficient manufacturing methods could influence whether promising solar materials can move from lab demonstrations toward practical use.

discovery.title: A wearable monitor aims to track wildfire smoke on wildlife
discovery.summary: Researchers developed an open-source air-quality monitor that can be attached to animal collars to measure particulate exposure and study wildlife behavior during smoke events.
discovery.why_it_matters: Better exposure data could clarify how wildfire smoke affects animals and help connect ecosystem impacts with risks to nearby communities.

discovery.title: A genetic adaptation gave butterflies richer color vision
discovery.summary: Research announced October 8 describes a genetic adaptation that produced an additional photoreceptor in butterflies, expanding the colors they can perceive and potentially helping them find nectar and other butterflies.
discovery.why_it_matters: The finding connects tiny genetic changes to animal behavior, pollination and how species experience their environments.

discovery.title: A robot dog reportedly ran a marathon on one battery charge
discovery.summary: A South Korean robot dog completed a marathon on a single battery charge, prompting researchers to explain how its design and energy use supported the feat.
discovery.why_it_matters: Longer-lasting mobile robots could affect inspection, delivery and emergency-response work, though a marathon demonstration alone does not prove readiness for routine deployment.
